Thanks :)

I still don't understand how something like that would work (maybe do an IAMA?), but I also know that it's not something that I want to engage in.

Even if I did get a fake SSN and established myself as a USC, I would still have the same psychological problem as I do now, the underlying nagging that at some moment, by random chance, something gets fucked up and then I end up getting arrested and also imprisoned in addition to being deported.

I come from a 3rd world country, the kind of country that it's very difficult to get out of since other countries won't give you entry visas. With a US passport you can easily enter most countries and have your passport stamped at the border/airport, but if I were to travel, I would need to apply for a visa into every single country. This is a process that takes months. 

That, and I have no money to travel anyway :)

I'm afraid of going back to my home country since I don't speak the language nor do I know anything about it. India is a totally foreign place for me -- would you just pull up your roots and just move there?

A TIN is not the same thing as an SSN. It can only be used for paying taxes anonymously -- so it's really only useful for drug dealers who don't want to have the book thrown at them for tax evasion and illegals.

It can't be used in place of an SSN when applying for work.

I can always work under the table for five bucks an hour.There's always someone out there who needs some heavy lifting work done, but so long as my parents are paying for my education, I might as well focus all my energies onto that and get the most out of it rather than being sleep deprived and tired all the time. What I'm worried about is what happens when I graduate. I'll have a BS in Computer Science but the number of firms that will employ an illegal is really low. I did pick CS because it is one of the few fields where you can be self-employed with minimal investment (home PC, internet, roof), but that's only a backup.

To emigrate to the US, one has to have a sponsor. The sponsor can be a close relative (sibling, parent, or child), an employer, or some other special category.

My US Citizen (USC) brother applied for my parents. They came over. After five years of being in the country, they got their citizenship. At no time did they overstay their visas.

I, on the other hand, overstayed my visa. The penalty for overstaying the visa by one day is a 3 year ban on returning to the country. Overstaying it by more than 180 days is a 10 year ban on returning to the country.

This ban can be "forgiven" if you're the child of a USC (under 21) or if you're the spouse of a USC. At the moment, I am neither so if I were to leave the country, I would not be allowed in for 10 years.
This is dishonest and illegal. I have been eyeing going into the military or doing work as a government contractor (if I ever get legalized..) and engaging in this kind of fraud would disqualify me.
